subject: math
title: Perimeter of Polygons
seo_title: Grade 3 Perimeter Worksheets: Add the Sides, Rectangles, Missing Sides and Word Problems
standard_text: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 perimeter worksheets with pictures: count units around a shape, add side lengths, perimeter of rectangles and squares, find a missing side, and perimeter vs. area word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Perimeter = the distance around. Add every side.
key_sub: A rectangle has 4 sides, even when only 2 numbers are shown: length + width + length + width. Perimeter is a length (cm, ft). Area is square units.
body_html:
What perimeter means

Perimeter is the distance all the way around a flat shape. Imagine an ant walking along every edge until it gets back to where it started. Perimeter is measured in units of length: cm, in, m or ft.

Add every side

For any shape with straight sides, add the lengths of all the sides. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

Rectangles and squares

Opposite sides of a rectangle are the same length, so a picture often shows only two numbers. You still have to add four sides.

ShapeHow to find the perimeterPerimeter
Rectangle 6 ft by 4 ft6 + 4 + 6 + 420 ft
Square with 7 cm sides4 × 728 cm
Hexagon with 5 in sides6 × 530 in
Example

A rectangle is 8 m long and 3 m wide. What is its perimeter?

8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22. Shortcut: 8 + 3 = 11, and 11 + 11 = 22.

Answer: 22 m

Find a missing side

If you know the perimeter, add the sides you know and subtract from the perimeter.

Example

A triangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. Two sides are 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the third side?

6 + 8 = 14. 20 − 14 = 6.

Answer: 6 cm

Example

A rectangle has a perimeter of 18 ft. It is 5 ft long. How wide is it?

Two lengths: 5 + 5 = 10. 18 − 10 = 8 for the two widths. 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

Answer: 4 ft

Same area, different perimeter

Two rectangles can cover the same space but have different edges.

RectangleAreaPerimeter
1 by 1212 sq units26 units
2 by 612 sq units16 units
3 by 412 sq units14 units

The long, thin rectangle has the most edge. The one closest to a square has the least.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding only the two numbers shown (6 + 4 = 10)A rectangle has 4 sides: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20
Multiplying length × widthThat is the area. Perimeter adds the sides
Skipping a side of a shapeTouch and count each side as you add it
Writing sq cmPerimeter is a length: cm, not sq cm

faq.q: What is perimeter in 3rd grade math?
faq.a: Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a flat shape. Add the lengths of all the sides. A rectangle that is 6 cm by 4 cm has a perimeter of 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm.

faq.q: What is the difference between perimeter and area?
faq.a: Perimeter is the length around the edge, measured in units such as cm or ft. Area is the space inside, measured in square units such as sq cm or sq ft.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side when you know the perimeter?
faq.a: Add the sides you know, then subtract that sum from the perimeter. For a rectangle, subtract the two known sides and divide what is left by 2.

faq.q: Can two rectangles have the same area but different perimeters?
faq.a: Yes. A 2 by 6 rectangle and a 3 by 4 rectangle both have an area of 12 square units, but their perimeters are 16 and 14 units.

items.q: Ava wants to put a fence around a garden that is 9 meters long and 6 meters wide. How many meters of fence are needed?
items.e: The fence goes all the way around: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m.

items.q: Sam glues ribbon around the edge of a square picture frame. Each side is 8 inches. How much ribbon is needed?
items.e: 4 equal sides: 4 × 8 = 32 inches.

items.q: A park is shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 120 m, 150 m and 90 m. Leo walks once around the park. How far does he walk?
items.e: Add the 3 sides: 120 + 150 + 90 = 360 m.

items.q: A rug is 7 feet long and 5 feet wide. Trim is sewn around all of its edges. How many feet of trim are used?
items.e: Perimeter = 7 + 5 + 7 + 5 = 24 ft. (35 sq ft would be the area of the rug.)

items.q: A rabbit pen is 10 feet long and 4 feet wide. One long side is against a wall, so it needs no fence. How many feet of fence are needed for the other 3 sides?
items.e: Only 3 sides get fence: 10 + 4 + 4 = 18 ft.

items.q: Jack used 30 feet of fence to go around a rectangular dog run. The dog run is 9 feet long. How wide is it?
items.e: Two lengths: 9 + 9 = 18. 30 − 18 = 12 for two widths. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 ft.

items.q: A square playground has sides of 25 meters. A coach runs around it 2 times. How far does the coach run?
items.e: Once around is 4 × 25 = 100 m. Two times around is 100 + 100 = 200 m.

items.q: A sign has 5 sides: 6, 6, 4, 4, 5 inches. What is the perimeter of the sign?
items.e: Add all 5 sides: 6 + 6 + 4 + 4 + 5 = 25 inches.

items.q: A classroom table is 30 inches long and 20 inches wide. Noah puts tape around the top edge. A roll has 120 inches of tape. Is one roll enough?
items.e: Perimeter = 30 + 20 + 30 + 20 = 100 inches. 100 is less than 120, so one roll is enough. (600 is the area. 50 is only one length and one width.)

items.q: A garden shaped like a hexagon has 6 equal sides. The fence around it is 24 meters long. How long is each side?
items.e: 6 equal sides share the 24 meters: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 m.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 20 units?
items.e: 2 + 8 + 2 + 8 = 20. A quick way: length + width must be half of 20, which is 10.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 24 units?

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 18 units?

items.q: Rectangle A is 2 by 9 units. Rectangle B is 3 by 6 units. Both have an area of 18 square units. Which has the greater perimeter?
items.e: A: 2 + 9 + 2 + 9 = 22 units. B: 3 + 6 + 3 + 6 = 18 units. Same area does not mean same perimeter. The long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: Rectangle A is 1 by 12 units. Rectangle B is 3 by 4 units. Both have an area of 12 square units. Which has the greater perimeter?
items.e: A: 1 + 12 + 1 + 12 = 26 units. B: 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = 14 units. Same area does not mean same perimeter. The long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 by 7 units. Rectangle B is 5 by 5 units. Both have a perimeter of 20 units. Which has the greater area?
items.e: A: 3 × 7 = 21 square units. B: 5 × 5 = 25 square units. Same perimeter does not mean same area. The shape closer to a square holds more space.

items.q: Rectangle A is 2 by 8 units. Rectangle B is 4 by 6 units. Both have a perimeter of 20 units. Which has the greater area?
items.e: A: 2 × 8 = 16 square units. B: 4 × 6 = 24 square units. Same perimeter does not mean same area. The shape closer to a square holds more space.
